lead: Quarries, steep slopes and a long tradition of self-building and community action.
text: Its name comes from the rock quarries on the hill, which supplied the materials used to build the city, and streets such as Carrer de la Cantera and Camí Vell de la Pedrera recall them. Until the mid-20th century the area was barely developed, and in the 1950s waves of immigrants arrived: many houses on the hillside were self-built, and between 1964 and 1967 residents laid the sewers and running water themselves through the "Urbanizar en domingo" (Developing on Sundays) initiative.

That community spirit lives on, with the Ateneu Popular de Nou Barris, centred on circus arts, the Parc del Pla de Fornells, on a former industrial site, and Roquetes station on line 3. At 2,465 €/m² and 701 €/month, it is a neighbourhood with moderate prices.
housing: Hillside houses, some of them self-built, and blocks of small flats from the 1950s.
